card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning if the index contains no legacy entries. When a requested transaction is in a pruned block, RPC and REST error responses return candidate block hashes so users can download them via getblockfrompeer and retry. Additionally, getrawtransaction with verbosity 2 gracefully omits fee and prevout data instead of failing when undo data is absent for refetched blocks. This resolves four long-standing feature requests dating back to 2017 (#10609, #12651, #16182, #35240).
changed_since_previous: No structural changes to the approach; the branch has been rebased with minor refactoring and updated release notes.
evidence: Resolves four long-standing issues requesting pruned txindex functionality dating back to 2017: #10609, #12651, #16182, and #35240 (PR description)
Builds directly on #35531, which switched txindex from recording raw disk file offsets to storing containing block hashes (PR description)
problem: Nodes with limited disk space running in pruned mode cannot enable -txindex, forcing anyone needing transaction lookups, PSBT input resolution, or proof generation to store hundreds of gigabytes of raw block data.

risk.why: Mistakes in index lookup logic or error reporting could return false misses or crash RPC endpoints when querying transactions across pruned block boundaries.

scope_notes: Adds an optional 'data' field to JSONRPCError to carry structured error payloads such as pruned_block_hashes, and introduces a TxLookupResult variant across index and node transaction lookup helpers.
summary: Allows running the transaction index (-txindex) on pruned nodes, provided the index contains no legacy format entries. When a transaction lookup targets a pruned block, the index and RPC/REST interfaces return the missing block hash so callers can fetch it on demand via getblockfrompeer and retry.
